argument_summary: The present record does not support an unqualified finding that certification is already compliant, but it does support a narrow certification path tied to the policy predicate itself. Admissible evidence shows the release clears aggregate readiness by 2.4 points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, while the current health-plan benefits slice is 1.5 points below the warning threshold. The controlling policy does not require that weakness to be eliminated before certification if it is instead disclosed in current release documentation or covered by approved mitigation. Because there is no approved risk acceptance in the record, the supportable position is conditional certification only if the current model card is updated to reflect the current eval batch and expressly disclose the health-plan benefits limitation before launch. On that framing, escalation beyond a caveated compliance treatment is unnecessary.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to justify the policy position. The relevant governance point is that a bounded caveat addresses the identified gap without unnecessary escalation beyond what the admissible record supports.
claims_about_policy: The policy is explicit that certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation. The admissible record already establishes that prior approval and informal monitoring are contextual only, so they should not be treated as substitutes. The actor is not defending clean compliance on the current stale documentation; the narrower claim is that the policy itself permits certification once the documentation condition is satisfied, and the auditor can treat the matter as caveated compliance rather than outright noncompliance if certification is conditioned on that update.
concessions: The current record does not support present-tense clean compliance because the model card is not yet shown to reflect the current eval batch.
There is no approved mitigation or formal risk-acceptance record covering the health-plan benefits regression.
Prior approval from nine weeks ago and the informal monitoring comment cannot cure the current documentation gap under the stated policy.
Public model-card and monitoring guidance is supplementary and cannot override the internal certification predicate.
